description: The MIROC7 atmospheric component is based on the CCSR-NIES atmospheric general circulation model (AGCM; Numaguti et al., 1997), which has been developed through successive versions of the MIROC climate model (e.g., Watanabe et al., 2010; Tatebe et al., 2019). It uses a spectral dynamical core with T85 horizontal resolution (~1.4°) and a hybrid σ–p vertical coordinate with 90 levels and a model top at 0.004 hPa. Physical parameterizations include radiation (Sekiguchi and Nakajima, 2008), turbulence (Nakanishi and Niino, 2004), convection (Chikira and Sugiyama, 2010; Park and Bretherton, 2009), large-scale condensation (Watanabe et al., 2009), and gravity-wave drag (McFarlane, 1987; Hines, 1997). In MIROC7, the radiation and cloud physics have been updated, including prognostic precipitation (Michibata et al., 2019) and a new stratocumulus-cloud parameterization (Kawai et al., 2019).
